The authoritative status is that the Teams integration is **in "Active Design and Planning"**, with a release target of **Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release)**; it is **not** done or ready for deployment [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. Currently, only the Slack connector is available as a limited pilot [NL-014#NL-014-S07].

The Slack thread is explicitly categorized as **informal, low-authority internal developer discussion** and not official documentation or policy; the Product Roadmap (NL-014) is the stated source of truth [NL-027#NL-027-S01]. The claims in that thread that the integration is "basically right around the corner" are contradicted by the CTO, engineering, and product management, who note it is strictly a future release, lacks security controls, tenant isolation, SSO, and citation formatting [NL-027#NL-027-S03], [NL-027#NL-027-S05]. Furthermore, NL-014 explicitly warns that sales playbooks and informal communications (like the Slack thread) may suggest readiness but must be clarified as future releases [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. Related sales overclaims in NL-023 are explicitly flagged as overclaims against the official roadmap [NL-023#NL-023-S04], and product management confirms the integration remains in the design phase for Q4, with development slated for early 2027 [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

Therefore, the Slack thread's statement is an overclaim; the authoritative status is **design/planning phase, not done**.
